title: clarify-credential-lookup-and-add-light-async-iterable-facade-cross-sdk
author: Leah Chen
description: Motivation: SDK users across Python/TypeScript/Go reported inconsistent credential resolution ordering and awkward ergonomics for streaming consumers. This PR centralizes credential lookup precedence for all SDKs (explicit config -> env vars -> shared OS credential cache -> platform delegated token) and introduces a lightweight async-iterable facade / sync-generator adapter to improve ergonomics for common streaming patterns. The change is intentionally conservative: no breaking changes to existing method names, but we add a small opt-in compatibility shim and bump SDK minor versions. Key changes: unify credential lookup precedence in client factory and document it; implement implicit credential fallthrough with deterministic logging and telemetry tag so operators can see which source won; introduce `AsyncIterableFacade` in TS that normalizes chunk framing, backpressure hints, and reconnect metadata; add `sync_stream()` helper in Python that wraps async iterators with a stable generator-based API for sync code paths; add a Go `streamer` helper that returns a context-aware channel iterator with explicit Cancel semantics and a small connection-warmup path; add a new retry preset `balanced` for streaming idempotency trade-offs and map it into all SDKs; small telemetry/trace tag harmonization so streaming spans include `cred_source` and `retry_preset`; update tests and examples; bump SDK versions. Testing/CI: unit tests (py/ts/go) and cross-language integration test harness run in CI; a flaky TS chunking test failed initially and was fixed by increasing a short debounce window and adding deterministic stub for chunk boundaries in tests. Commits are organized as small, reviewable pieces (credential lookup, TS facade, Python helper, Go streamer, tests & docs, version bumps). Backwards compatibility: opt-in facade and helpers; existing streaming APIs remain supported. Merge: squash and merge after approvals and a green CI run.
